newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait hopes no need to dissolve parliament.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait hopes no need to dissolve parliament.

text.p: Kuwait's Prime Minister Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah expressed hope in remarks published on Tuesday that tension between parliament and his government would not lead to the dissolution of the elected house.

"God willing matters would not lead to that end," Sheikh Saad, who is also crown prince, told al-Qabas daily when asked if MPs' continued "aggravation and use of harsh tone" with ministers would lead to parliament's dissolution.
According to the constitution, Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah can dissolve the house and call for new elections upon the prime minister's recommendation.
"Our brother deputies developed an obsession when you (in the press) wrote that this is a governmental assembly...They wanted to erase this so they began to aggravate things," Sheikh Saad said.

Citing security and other concerns at the height of the nearby 1980-88 Iran-Iraq war, the emir dissolved parliament in 1986. Parliamentary life was restored a year after the 1991 U.S.-led Gulf War to free Kuwait of seven months of Iraqi occupation.

Although the current parliament, elected in October, is seen as less confrontational than the previous opposition-dominated house, there have been media reports about irritation with the tone used by some MPs in their criticism of the government.
Sheikh Saad said he planned to meet MPs in the coming weeks to discuss "unifying ranks". He did not elaborate.
